mainTopic: Bed parts and worn scraps as סכך, hollowing out a גדיש, and hanging walls (מחיצה תלויה)
overview: This amud continues a discussion of a משנה in מסכת כלים about a bed (מטה). רבי אליעזר and חכמים disagree whether a bed can become טמא while it is taken apart. The גמרא explains which bed pieces still count as כלים: a side board with its two legs, which can be leaned on a wall and strung with ropes to sit on. This matters for סוכה because anything that can become טמא is פסול as סכך. The גמרא then turns to רבי אמי בר טביומי, who rules that worn-out scraps of כלים are פסול as סכך. אביי defines these scraps, and a ברייתא about leftover mat pieces and reed mats supports רבי אמי. Next, רב הונא limits the משנה about hollowing out a גדיש: it is a kosher סוכה if a space one טפח high over seven טפחים already existed. This is shown in two versions, first as a proof and then as an answer to a contradiction. Finally, a new משנה discusses walls lowered from above. The גמרא explains that רבי יוסי and חכמים disagree about whether a מחיצה תלויה works, and it begins citing a משנה from עירובין about a cistern, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A מחלוקת about whether a dismantled bed can become impure
steps.stepSummary: A משנה (כלים 18:9) records a dispute. רבי אליעזר holds that a bed becomes טמא and טהור only as a complete unit. חכמים hold that it becomes טמא and טהור even in its separate parts.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bed becomes impure as a whole unit and becomes pure as a whole unit. These are the words of רבי אליעזר. The חכמים say: it becomes impure in parts and becomes pure in parts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of quoting a משנה from מסכת כלים, where רבי אליעזר and חכמים disagree about a bed that is taken apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אליעזר, a bed is a כלי only when it is assembled, so its separate pieces cannot become טמא. According to חכמים, the separate pieces are still a כלי and can become טמא. For סוכה, anything that can become טמא may not be used as סכך, so this dispute decides whether bed parts may go on the roof.

keyTerms.meaning: A bed
A bundle, meaning the bed as one assembled unit
Limbs or parts, meaning the bed's separate pieces
Becomes טמא (ritually impure)
Becomes טהור (ritually pure) through טבילה

steps.whyThisMatters: סכך must be something that cannot become טמא. Whether bed parts can become טמא therefore decides whether they may be used as סכך.

phrases.english: A bed becomes impure as a whole unit
and becomes pure as a whole unit,
phrases.notes: It must be assembled to receive or lose impurity.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
And the Sages say:
it becomes impure in parts and becomes pure in parts.
phrases.notes: Even when it is dismantled.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִטָּה מְטַמֵּאת חֲבִילָה וּמְטַהֶרֶת חֲבִילָה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from the previous amud. There the גמרא cited this משנה from מסכת כלים to explain the law about a dismantled bed used as סכך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: a bed becomes טמא and טהור only when assembled. חכמים: it becomes טמא and טהור even in its parts.

steps.title: Which bed parts do the Sages mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly the 'parts' mentioned by חכמים are.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are they?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question to define the 'parts' in the opinion of חכמים. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bed that is completely smashed into useless pieces is certainly no longer a כלי. So חכמים must mean specific pieces that are still useful. The גמרא wants to know which pieces those are.

keyTerms.meaning: What are they? A request for a definition

phrases.english: What are they?
phrases.notes: Which 'parts' do the Sages mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of a term used by חכמים in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which specific bed parts the חכמים mean when they say a bed becomes טמא 'in parts'.

steps.title: A long side with two legs and a short side with two legs
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנן, quoting רבי, explains that the parts are a long board with its two legs still attached, and a short board with its two legs still attached.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנן said in the name of רבי: a long side with two legs, and a short side with two legs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by naming the exact pieces: a side board that still has its two legs attached.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A frame side that keeps its two legs is not useless junk. It can still be propped up and put to use, as step 5 explains. Loose boards or loose legs would not count.

keyTerms.meaning: The long side board of the bed frame
The short side board of the bed frame
Legs

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanan said that Rabbi (Yehuda HaNasi) said:
a long side and two legs,
phrases.notes: The legs are still attached to it.

phrases.english: a short side and two legs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'parts' are a long side with two attached legs and a short side with two attached legs.

steps.title: What use do these pieces have?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what these pieces are good for, since a כלי must have some use.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are they fit for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what practical use these pieces have that would make them count as a כלי. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something can become טמא only if it is a usable כלי. A side board with two legs is not a bed by itself. So the גמרא needs to show that it still has a real use.

keyTerms.meaning: For what is it fit? What is it good for?

phrases.english: For what are they fit?
phrases.notes: What use makes them a vessel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the answer of step 3. Why would these pieces still count as a כלי?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical use the bed pieces have that keeps them in the category of a כלי.

steps.title: Lean them on a wall, string ropes, and sit on them
steps.stepSummary: The pieces can be leaned against a wall with ropes strung across them, which makes a usable seat.
steps.simpleTranslation: To lean them against a wall, sit on them, and stretch ropes across them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the pieces can be leaned on a wall and strung with ropes to make something you can sit on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each piece can stand on its two legs while it leans against the wall. Once ropes are stretched across, it works as a makeshift seat. Because it can still serve as something to sit on, it is a כלי and can become טמא, as חכמים say.

keyTerms.meaning: Against the wall
To sit
Ropes

steps.whatToRemember: According to חכמים, a side of a bed with its two legs is still a usable כלי. It can become טמא, so it may not be used as סכך.

phrases.english: To lean them against the wall
and to sit on them
and to stretch ropes across them.
phrases.notes: The ropes form a seat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The pieces can be leaned on a wall and strung with ropes to make a seat, so they remain usable כלים.

steps.title: רבי אמי: roofing with worn-out vessel scraps is invalid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the statement of רבי אמי בר טביומי, which was quoted earlier: a סוכה roofed with worn-out remnants of כלים is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Returning to the matter itself: רבי אמי בר טביומי said, if someone roofed the סוכה with worn-out remnants of vessels, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is going back to examine a statement it quoted earlier. Here that statement is the ruling of רבי אמי בר טביומי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These worn scraps are often too small to become טמא anymore. Even so, רבי אמי rules them פסול because they came from כלים. This is a rabbinic extra stringency.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself. The גמרא returns to analyze a statement quoted earlier
He roofed it (the סוכה) with סכך
Worn-out remnants of vessels or garments
Invalid

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume these scraps are פסול because they can still become טמא. As אביי's definition in step 8 shows, they are too small for that. They are פסול only because of where they came from.

phrases.english: Returning to the matter itself,
Rabbi Ami bar Tavyomei said:
If one roofed it with worn-out remnants of vessels, it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי בַּר טַבְיוֹמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the bed discussion and goes back to a statement that was cited earlier in the sugya.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוכה roofed with worn-out remnants of כלים is פסול.

steps.title: What counts as 'worn-out vessels'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a definition of בלאי כלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are worn-out remnants of vessels?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what exactly is meant by בלאי כלים. This sets up the definition from אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the scraps were large enough to become טמא, being פסול would be obvious. So the גמרא wants to know how small the scraps are and what makes them 'worn out'.

keyTerms.meaning: What?

phrases.english: What are worn-out remnants of vessels?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the term used in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact definition of בלאי כלים.

steps.title: אביי: scraps of cloth smaller than three by three fingerbreadths
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that these are small pieces of cloth less than three by three fingerbreadths. They are useless to both poor and rich people.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: small cloths that are not three by three fingerbreadths, which are not useful to the poor or to the rich.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defines worn-out vessels as tiny scraps of cloth that are too small for anyone to use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cloth becomes טמא only if it is large enough to be useful, and the smallest such size is three by three fingerbreadths. Scraps smaller than that cannot become טמא at all. Even so, רבי אמי rules them פסול as סכך, which shows his ruling is a rabbinic stringency based on their origin as כלים.

keyTerms.meaning: Small rags or patches of cloth
Three by three (fingerbreadths)
Poor people
Rich people

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: מַטְלָנִיּוֹת שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ,
phrases.english: small cloths that do not measure three by three (fingerbreadths),
which are not fit
neither for the poor nor for the rich.
phrases.notes: No one would bother to use them, so they cannot become טמא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מַטְלָנִיּוֹת שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Scraps of cloth smaller than three by three fingerbreadths, which are useless to everyone.

steps.title: A ברייתא about mat remnants supports רבי אמי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that leftover pieces of a mat made of שיפא or גמי may not be used as סכך. This is true even though they are now smaller than the size needed to become טמא. This matches the view of רבי אמי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with רבי אמי בר טביומי: a mat made of papyrus or reed grass, its remnants, even though they were reduced below its required size, one may not roof with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the ruling of רבי אמי בר טביומי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The remnants of the mat are too small to become טמא, just like the cloth scraps in step 8. Even so, the ברייתא forbids using them as סכך. This shows that something that was once a כלי stays פסול even after it can no longer become טמא, exactly as רבי אמי said.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught in line with his view. Introduces a supporting source
A woven mat
A type of rush or papyrus
Reed grass
Its remnants
The minimum size needed to become טמא

steps.whatToRemember: Remnants of כלים are פסול as סכך even when they are too small to become טמא. This is the view of רבי אמי בר טביומי, and the ברייתא about mats supports it.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי בַּר טַבְיוֹמֵי:
phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rabbi Ami bar Tavyomei:
a mat made of papyrus and of reed grass,
its remnants,
even though they were reduced below its required size,
phrases.notes: They are now too small to become טמא.

phrases.english: one may not roof with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי בַּר טַבְיוֹמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that supports the ruling of step 6 as defined in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling of רבי אמי בר טביומי that worn-out remnants of כלים are פסול as סכך.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא forbidding the use of mat remnants as סכך even after they are too small to become טמא.

steps.title: Large reed mats may be used as roofing, small ones may not
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. A large reed mat may be used as סכך and a small one may not. רבי אליעזר holds that even a large mat can become טמא and so may not be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: A mat made of reeds: if it is large, one may use it as סכך. If it is small, one may not. רבי אליעזר says: even a large one can become טמא, so one may not use it as סכך.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step keeps going. It now rules about mats made of reeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A large mat is normally made for roofing, not for lying on, so it is not considered a כלי and may be used as סכך. A small mat is made for sitting or sleeping, so it counts as a כלי that can become טמא, and כלים are פסול for סכך. רבי אליעזר disagrees and treats even a large mat as a כלי that can become טמא, so it is also פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: A woven mat
Reeds
We may use it to roof the סוכה (as סכך)
Can become ritually impure, which is the sign that it counts as a כלי

steps.confusionAlert: The size is not what matters in itself. Size only tells us what the mat is normally used for. A large mat is for roofing, while a small mat is for lying on, and lying on it is what makes it a כלי.

phrases.english: A mat of reeds, if large: one may roof with it,
phrases.notes: A large mat is usually made for shade or roofing, not for lying on.

phrases.english: if small: one may not roof with it.
phrases.notes: A small mat is made for lying on, so it counts as a כלי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
even it (the large one) can become impure,
and one may not roof with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the rest of the same ברייתא that was brought in step 9 to support רבי אמי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the ת״ק, a large reed mat is kosher as סכך and a small one is not. According to רבי אליעזר, both are not kosher because both can become טמא.

steps.title: רב הונא limits the משנה about hollowing out a grain stack
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's case of hollowing out a גדיש, רב הונא says it is not a סוכה only when there was no existing space one טפח high over seven טפחים. If there was such a space, it is a kosher סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says that one who hollows out a stack of grain has not made a סוכה. רב הונא said: they only taught this where there was no open space one טפח high stretching over seven טפחים. But if there was an open space one טפח high stretching over seven טפחים, it is a סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה: someone digs out a space inside a pile of grain to make a סוכה. רב הונא explains that the משנה's ruling of 'not a סוכה' applies only in a limited case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's problem is that the roof was not placed as סכך. The person only dug out space underneath grain that was already lying there. רב הונא says that if there was already a real space under the grain, one טפח high over the minimum סוכה area of seven טפחים, then the grain was a roof over a space from the start. Digging just deepens that space, so it is kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: One who hollows or digs out
A stack or heap of harvested grain
'They only taught this when…', which limits a ruling to a specific case
An empty space one handbreadth high
Stretching over seven handbreadths, the minimum size of a סוכה

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up רב הונא's distinction, which the rest of this passage supports and then uses to settle a contradiction.

phrases.english: "One who hollows out a grain stack."
phrases.notes: These words quote the line of the משנה that the גמרא is about to discuss.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
They only taught this
where there is not there a space of a handbreadth
stretching over seven (handbreadths),

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יֵשׁ שָׁם חָלָל טֶפַח בְּמֶשֶׁךְ שִׁבְעָה —
phrases.english: but if there is there a space of a handbreadth stretching over seven —
this is a sukkah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This begins a new topic from the משנה, separate from the discussion of mats and בלאי כלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hollowing out a גדיש does not make a סוכה, unless there was already a space one טפח high over seven טפחים. In that case it is kosher.

steps.title: A ברייתא says hollowing out a grain stack does make a סוכה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is brought that says one who hollows out a גדיש to make a סוכה has made a valid סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: one who hollows out a stack of grain to make himself a סוכה, this is a סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רב הונא. This is the first part of a proof that the next steps will finish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'it is a סוכה' with no conditions at all. On its own, this seems to clash with the משנה. The גמרא is about to point out that clash and use it to prove רב הונא's point.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was also taught this way in a ברייתא', the formula for bringing support
To make himself a סוכה

phrases.english: It was also taught this way (in a baraita):
One who hollows out a grain stack to make himself a sukkah —
this is a sukkah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This begins a proof for רב הונא's distinction.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's claim that hollowing out a גדיש can sometimes make a kosher סוכה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that rules 'it is a סוכה'.

steps.title: But the משנה says it is not a סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא seems to contradict the משנה, which says it is not a סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in the משנה that it is not a סוכה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction between the ברייתא and the משנה. This is a setup move: it shows the two sources cannot both be about the same case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'not a סוכה' and the ברייתא says 'it is a סוכה' about what looks like the same case. This question is not meant to knock down the ברייתא. It forces us to say that the two sources describe different cases, and that is exactly what the next step uses.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But didn't we learn in the משנה…?', which points to a clashing source
It is not a valid סוכה

phrases.english: But didn't we learn (in the mishnah)
"it is not a sukkah"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This shows that the ברייתא from step 12 clashes with the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain reading that the ברייתא and the משנה are talking about the same case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two sources give opposite rulings on what looks like one case, so there must be some difference between them.

steps.title: So the ברייתא proves רב הונא is right
steps.stepSummary: The only way to fit the two sources together is רב הונא's distinction, so the ברייתא proves him right.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it true that we learn from this as רב הונא said? Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. The ברייתא must be talking about a case with an existing one-טפח space, just as רב הונא said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (not a סוכה) is about a case with no existing space. The ברייתא (a סוכה) is about a case where there was a space one טפח high over seven טפחים. The גמרא accepts this proof with the words 'שמע מינה'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, isn't it…?', which introduces the only way to explain the sources
'Learn from it', meaning the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: משנה = no existing space, so not a סוכה. ברייתא = an existing space one טפח high over seven טפחים, so it is a סוכה. That is רב הונא's distinction, and the ברייתא proves it.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not so,
learn from it as Rav Huna said.
Indeed, learn from it.
phrases.notes: The גמרא agrees that the proof works.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ כִּדְרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This settles the clash from step 13 by using רב הונא's distinction, which completes the proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב הונא's distinction is proven by the ברייתא.

steps.title: Second version: the משנה and ברייתא contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, people present the משנה and the ברייתא as a contradiction rather than as a proof for רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some raised it as a contradiction. We learned in the משנה: one who hollows out a stack of grain to make himself a סוכה, it is not a סוכה. But it was taught in a ברייתא: this is a סוכה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of the same discussion. Here the clash between the משנה and the ברייתא is asked as a question, and רב הונא answers it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רב הונא spoke first and the ברייתא was brought as support. In this version, the clash comes first as a problem, and רב הונא's distinction is the answer. The halacha comes out the same. Only the order of the discussion is different.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Some raised it as a contradiction', which introduces a second version of the discussion
'But it was taught in a ברייתא…', which brings a clashing source

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the same material told in a different order. In the first version רב הונא's rule was proven, and in this version it is used to answer a question.

phrases.english: There are those who raise it as a contradiction.
We learned (in the mishnah):
One who hollows out a grain stack to make himself a sukkah —
it is not a sukkah.
But it was taught (in a baraita):
"this is a sukkah"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This retells steps 11–14 in a different way, starting with the contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain readings of the משנה and the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says 'not a סוכה' and the ברייתא says 'a סוכה' about the same act of hollowing out a גדיש.

steps.title: רב הונא: each source is talking about a different case
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the ברייתא is about a case with an existing space one טפח high over seven טפחים, and the משנה is about a case without one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: it is not difficult. Here (the ברייתא) is where there is a space one טפח high over seven טפחים. There (the משנה) is where there is no space one טפח high over seven טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא settles the contradiction by assigning each source to a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no real disagreement between the sources. If a one-טפח space over seven טפחים already existed under the grain, digging just enlarges it, so it is a kosher סוכה. Without such a space, the whole סוכה space is made by digging under grain that was never placed as סכך, so it is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not difficult', the opening of an answer
'Here… there', which splits two sources into two different cases

steps.whatToRemember: Hollowing out a גדיש makes a kosher סוכה only if a space one טפח high over seven טפחים was already there before the digging.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: it is not difficult:
here, where there is there a space of a handbreadth
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא, which rules it is a סוכה.

phrases.english: stretching over seven,
there, where there is not there a space of a handbreadth
phrases.notes: This is the משנה, which rules it is not a סוכה.

phrases.english: stretching over seven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the contradiction raised in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different physical situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא disagree about the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a case with an existing space one טפח high over seven טפחים, so it is kosher. The משנה is about a case with no such space, so it is פסול.

steps.title: New משנה: Walls lowered from above versus walls built from below
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a wall lowered from above is invalid if it stops 3 טפחים above the ground. A wall built up from the ground is valid once it reaches 10 טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone lowers the walls of a סוכה from the top down, and the bottom edge is 3 טפחים above the ground, the סוכה is invalid. If he builds from the bottom up, once the wall is 10 טפחים high, the סוכה is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives two rules about how a סוכה wall must be positioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wall hanging from the top that leaves a gap of 3 טפחים at the bottom is not a real wall, because small animals can slip underneath. A wall rising from the ground only needs to be 10 טפחים tall. It does not have to reach the roof at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the text being studied)
One who lowers or lets down
Walls (of the סוכה)
Handbreadths (a unit of measurement)
Invalid
Valid

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two numbers. The 3 טפחים is the GAP at the bottom of a hanging wall. The 10 טפחים is the HEIGHT of a wall standing on the ground.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who lowers walls from above downward,

phrases.aramaic: אִם גָּבוֹהַּ מִן הָאָרֶץ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים —
phrases.english: if it is three handbreadths above the ground —
phrases.notes: A gap of 3 טפחים lets small animals pass under, so it is not a wall.

phrases.english: it is invalid.
From below upward,
if it is ten handbreadths high — it is valid.
phrases.notes: It does not need to reach the סכך.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic after the גדיש discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wall hanging from above is invalid if it stops 3 טפחים above the ground. A wall built from below is valid once it is 10 טפחים high.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: A hanging wall only needs to be ten handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says a wall lowered from above is treated the same as a wall built from below. If it is 10 טפחים long, it is valid, even if it does not reach near the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Just as a wall from below upward needs 10 טפחים, so too a wall from above downward needs only 10 טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with the first opinion in the משנה about hanging walls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יוסי's view, the gap at the bottom does not matter. All that matters is that the wall itself measures 10 טפחים. So a 10-טפחים wall hanging in the air still counts as a full wall.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with the first opinion
Just as... so too (a comparison formula)
From above downward (a hanging wall)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Just as from below upward it is ten handbreadths,
so too from above downward it is ten handbreadths.
phrases.notes: The gap below a hanging wall does not invalidate it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמִּלְּמַטָּה לְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a disagreeing opinion about the hanging wall rule from Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hanging wall 10 טפחים long is valid regardless of how high it is off the ground.

steps.title: What is the root of the disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle the חכמים and רבי יוסי are arguing about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens and asks for the underlying reason behind the argument in the משנה. This question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on anyone. The גמרא simply wants to identify the general principle that splits the two opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
About what do they disagree?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the dispute in Steps 17 and 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle behind the dispute between the חכמים and רבי יוסי.

steps.title: The dispute is about whether a suspended partition counts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי holds that a מחיצה תלויה (a hanging partition) works like a real wall. The חכמים hold that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds that a suspended partition permits, and the other Sage holds that a suspended partition does not permit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The argument is about whether a wall hanging in the air counts as a real wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first 'מר' is רבי יוסי: a מחיצה תלויה is valid, so a hanging 10-טפחים wall works. The second 'מר' is the חכמים: a hanging wall does not count, so it must come down to within 3 טפחים of the ground. The word 'מתרת' (permits) is borrowed from the laws of carrying on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A suspended (hanging) partition that does not reach the ground
Permits (counts as a valid wall)
One Sage holds... and the other Sage holds

steps.confusionAlert: The text does not name who holds which view. The first 'מר' (says it permits) is רבי יוסי, and the second 'מר' (says it does not permit) is the חכמים.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of מחיצה תלויה becomes the key concept. The next source, about a cistern on שבת, is brought to test this principle.

phrases.english: One Sage holds a suspended partition permits,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַר סָבַר מְחִיצָה תְּלוּיָה אֵינָהּ מַתֶּרֶת.
phrases.english: and one Sage holds a suspended partition does not permit.
phrases.notes: This is the חכמים (the first opinion).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is whether a מחיצה תלויה is valid: רבי יוסי says yes, the חכמים say no.

steps.title: A related משנה: The cistern between two courtyards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from עירובין. It says water may be drawn on שבת from a cistern shared by two courtyards only if a 10-טפחים partition divides it, whether above, below, or within its rim. It then begins quoting רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: A cistern between two courtyards may not be drawn from on שבת unless a partition of 10 טפחים was made for it, whether above, below, or within its rim. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings in a different משנה about a hanging partition in a cistern. This is setting up a comparison to מחיצה תלויה, and the discussion continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Placing the partition 'above' (מלמעלה) means it hangs down toward the water without touching it. That is a מחיצה תלויה, and here the משנה says it works. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's words are cut off here; his opinion continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned there (in a different משנה)
A cistern or pit holding water
Courtyards
Draw (water)
Its rim (the edge of the cistern)
A תנא whose opinion is about to be quoted

steps.whyThisMatters: This source shows a case where a hanging partition is accepted. That links it directly to the dispute between רבי יוסי and the חכמים.

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: In משנה עירובין.

phrases.english: A cistern that is between two courtyards —
one may not draw from it on Shabbat

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עָשָׂה לָהּ מְחִיצָה עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים,
phrases.english: unless he made for it a partition of ten handbreadths,
whether above or below,

Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם: בּוֹר שֶׁבֵּין שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵירוֹת
